sentences.text:
Counsel for Petitioner :- Anil Kumar Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Nipun Singh,Sunil Kumar Misra Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
No one has put in appearance on behalf of petitioner to press the writ petition.
Sri Sumit Suri holding brief of Sri Nipun Singh has appeared on behalf of Uttar Pradesh Awas Vikas Parishad, learned Standing counsel for the State-respondent.
It is admitted fact of the matter that the award for the land in question has been declared in the year 2015.
As per own contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner the possession of land has been taken.
There is no explanation for the delay/laches in filing the writ petition after the period of more than seven years of the declaration of the award.

sentences.text: The issue herein has been considered in Writ C No. 3969 of 2022 in the light of the decision of the Apex Court in Indore Development Authority v. Manohar Lal 2020 (8) SCC 129.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority v. Manohar Lal 2020 (8) SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is noted therein that the Apex Court in Indore Development Authority (Supra) has held that if the possession of the land in question has been taken under the Land Acquisition Act, the tenure holders/land owners are entitled for the higher rate of compensation as provided under the Act,
2013 which came into force on 1.1.2014.

However, the provisions of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 would not be applicable in such situation where the possession of the land has already been taken much prior to the enforcement of the Act, 2013.

For the aforesaid reason, we do not find any merit in the writ petition and the same is accordingly,
dismissed.
